## Details

### `show macsec status [<ports>]`

Both ends must show MACsec and encryption enabled. If only one side is configured, the link usually carries no traffic.


### `show macsec mka participant [<ports>] [verbose]`

No live peer means a CKN/CAK mismatch, MKA disabled on the other side, or different profile settings.


### `show macsec statistics [<ports>] [secure channel {inbound | outbound}]`

Rising invalid or late counters point to replay-window or key problems. Reset them with `macsec clear-stats [port <ports>]`.


### `show macsec mka keychain [<name>]`

When the in-use key expires, the switch rolls over to the next key without traffic loss and logs "Participant switched to the next keychain key".


### `boot config flags macsec`

Get there: `enable` → `configure terminal`

Mutually exclusive with `boot config flags ipv6-egress-filter`. It only takes effect after save config and a reboot.

> ▲ **Caution:** Needs a reboot.


### `macsec connectivity-association <name> connectivity-association-key <cak>`

Get there: `enable` → `configure terminal`

```
macsec connectivity-association CA-CORE connectivity-association-key 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
interface gigabitEthernet 1/49
  macsec connectivity-association CA-CORE
  macsec encryption
  macsec enable
```

This example is static CAK mode (no MKA). The CA name is 5-32 characters, the key 10-64. Do not save real keys in this cheatsheet.


### `macsec mka profile <name>`

Get there: `enable` → `configure terminal`

```
macsec mka profile MKACORE
  confidentiality-offset 30
  include-sci enable
  replay-protect enable window-size 64
  exit
```

Profile names may only use letters and digits and are case sensitive.


### `macsec mka profile <name> / macsec mka enable (interface)`

Get there: `enable` → `configure terminal` → `interface gigabitEthernet <ports>`

```
interface gigabitEthernet 1/49
  macsec mka profile MKACORE
  macsec connectivity-association CA-CORE
  macsec mka enable
```

Order matters. Apply the MKA profile first, then the CA or keychain, then enable MKA. The 9.4 docs say that a port associated with a CA before it has an MKA profile cannot use MKA.


### `macsec mka keychain <name> / key <ckn> cak <cak> endtime <MMddyyyyhhmmss | unlimited>`

Get there: `enable` → `configure terminal` (also in MKA Keychain Config)

```
macsec mka keychain KC-CORE
  key KEY2026 cak <cak-2026> endtime 12312026235959
  key KEY2027 cak <cak-2027> endtime unlimited
  exit
interface gigabitEthernet 1/49
  macsec mka profile MKACORE
  macsec mka keychain KC-CORE
  macsec mka enable
```

The endtime is UTC, whatever the switch time zone is. The CKN/CAK pairs must match on both ends. You can change end times or add and delete keys while the keychain is in use. On the 5320 and 5420 Series, keychains are supported from 9.4.


### `macsec cipher-suite {gcm-aes-128 | gcm-aes-256 | gcm-aes-xpn-128 | gcm-aes-xpn-256}`

Get there: `enable` → `configure terminal` → `interface gigabitEthernet <ports>`

The XPN suites (9.3+, on 7830, 7520-48YE-8CE and 5720-VIM-2CE) avoid frequent SAK rekeying on fast links and need MKA. Both ends must use the same suite.


### `macsec confidentiality-offset <30 | 50>`

Get there: `enable` → `configure terminal` → `interface gigabitEthernet <ports>`
